clue.text: Textile fabric in production of gals' briefs

indicators.note: a production of these words makes something new from them, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A designer turns a pair of women's knickers into a new cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' is the anagram signal: GALS plus BRIEFS (the apostrophe adds no letter) rearrange into the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass fibre is woven into cloth and matting, so this material counts as a textile fabric.

clue.text: Company set up prize worker as resident

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up turns it to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cup is a trophy given as a prize
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A firm installs its award-winning employee as a live-in member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' is the reversal signal, fitting a down clue, where the letters read upwards. 'Company' looks like a business, but it only gives the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in or holds a place is its occupier, a resident.

parts.note: greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A confession: someone owned up to wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitted' reads as confessed, but the definition means conceded or consented to.
explanation.definitionFit: To have admitted a point is to have conceded or consented to it.

explanation.surface: Fissures appear in someone's lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are snide remarks, the same as cracks or jibes; digs is also British slang for rented lodgings.

clue.text: Committee in progress, covering City match

indicators.note: the committee and progress pieces sit around the city, covering it

parts.note: something going on, in progress, is said to be on
Paris is the capital city of France, the crossword's favourite city

explanation.surface: A committee meets while a big-city football match is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is the container signal: the two outer pieces sit together around the city. 'match' is the definition, as in 'there's no comparison' meaning 'no match'.
explanation.definitionFit: A match, as in 'no match for', is a likeness judged by setting two things side by side.

parts.note: an opera is a musical work, and opera is also the plural of opus, works

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word rule

explanation.surface: A telephone exchange where staff are working to rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' supplies OPERA, plural of opus; 'initially' takes R from 'rule'. The definition names the place by the person who runs it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who staffs a telephone switchboard and connects calls is the operator.

indicators.note: circling means the bird's letters go around the lake's letter

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird wheels over a lake with a duck on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like another bird beside the lake, but it is a verb, to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a blow is to dodge or recoil from it, the same as wincing away.

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an air is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: A piece of music for piano composed for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is two performers together, a couple or twosome.

clue.text: Mixed gin and tonic with nothing added? Unknown in Italy

indicators.note: mixed suggests a cocktail being stirred, and signals the letters of gin and tonic being stirred up

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone orders a gin and tonic made with no extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' is the anagram signal, the 'and' only joining the two drinks; the zero goes on the end. 'in Italy' tells the solver the word is Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word means unrecognised, and English uses it of someone travelling under a hidden identity.

clue.text: A thousand cut around in dance

indicators.note: around means the word for cut is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thousand were cut from a dance troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the word for cut back to front, giving POL; K for a thousand and the clue's opening A follow, written after the dance's start though printed first.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Bohemian couples' dance in two-four time became a ballroom craze in the 1840s.

indicators.note: outside means the airlines' word wraps around the letter for Russia

parts.note: an air line is a route flown by aircraft, so airlines are air routes
R is the international abbreviation for Russia

explanation.surface: Aircraft flying airline routes that skirt round Russian airspace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planes' suggests aircraft, but these are woodworking planes: a router cuts grooves in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a carpenter's tool, a kind of plane for hollowing out grooves.

clue.text: Fellow gets salmon without broken net

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the salmon word goes around the rest

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon

indicators.note: broken means the letters of net are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fisherman lands a salmon even though his net is torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old meaning of outside, not lacking; 'broken' scrambles the net to TNE. PARR is a young salmon still in fresh water.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow can be a companion or equal, an associate who shares in something.

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means splendid or first-rate; a grand is also the large horizontal piano.

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: An editor lengthened a sentence in a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks like grammar, but it is a jail term: a STRETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expanded has been pulled or extended beyond its former size.

clue.text: Old iron crate stacked with lamps

indicators.note: stacked suggests the letters are piled up in a new order

explanation.surface: A junk shop's old iron: a box piled high with lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stacked' rearranges CRATE plus LAMPS; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Old iron is metal fit only for melting down, discarded waste metal.

clue.text: Law-enforcers in Norfolk town drive out

indicators.note: in means the law-enforcers' word sits inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
a posse is a band summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law

explanation.surface: Lawmen in a Norfolk town force someone out of their home.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, in eastern England. 'in' puts the sheriff's bands inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict someone or strip them of property is to drive them out.

clue.text: Where to expect, in a way, a well-lit stage

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Where to expect, in a way, a well-lit stage', has no reading of 'well-lit' that leads to the phrase meaning a critical point of decision; the OCR looks garbled and no scan or reprint gives the true words.
annotationWithheld.clue: Where to expect, in a way, a well-lit stage

parts.note: extreme can mean wild or immoderate, as in extreme views

explanation.surface: Rugged, untamed hills in the south of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heights' looks like hills, but the definition means utmost points, as in 'the heights of folly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremes are the furthest limits or highest pitches of something, its peaks.

parts.note: reads as an estate agent's description of a run-down house, but describes the quality of being harsh or rugged

explanation.definitionFit: Harshness of surface or manner is a quality, a property in the scientific sense, of being very rough.

indicators.note: refitted means the letters are fitted together again in a new way

parts.note: the printed words fans and type, with the letter I the setter meant between them

explanation.surface: A fan's typewriter needs a clip to keep it together after a repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refitted' is the anagram signal and 'for' the join. As printed the fodder has only eight letters and lacks the I that SAFETY PIN needs, so a letter I has been lost where the comma stands.
explanation.definitionFit: This bent pin with a guarded point is a fastening for nappies and clothing.

clue.text: Decoration on spire completed in Ca? Not quite entirely

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Decoration on spire completed in Ca? Not quite entirely', is garbled: FINI (French for completed) plus AL needs a place such as France or Calais where 'Ca?' stands, and no scan or reprint gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Decoration on spire completed in Ca? Not quite entirely

clue.text: A priest for confirmation, in short

parts.note: taken as written
P is an abbreviation for priest, as in PP, parish priest
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A priest arrives to perform a confirmation service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confirmation' suggests the church rite, but here it means approval; 'in short' says the answer is the clipped form, as in goods sent 'on appro'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for approval: goods sent on approval may be returned if the buyer does not sanction them.

indicators.note: singular means odd or strange, so the letters of laurel are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: The charm of a single laurel bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like grammar (one, not many), but means peculiar and rearranges LAUREL.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractiveness, the power to charm or entice.

indicators.note: slotted in means the queen's letters are fitted inside the other word

parts.note: since means because
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen

explanation.surface: An honest admission: it is straight because the Queen has been fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight' means honest here, not level.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight answer is an honest one, genuine and frank.

clue.text: Lair located on edge of forest

parts.note: set means placed or located

indicators.note: edge of picks the last letter, the end edge of the word forest

explanation.surface: An animal's den found at the edge of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A SETT is a badger's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow of a badger, its den.

clue.text: Star, look, making comeback in capital

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the capital

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word for look comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A star makes a comeback appearance in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns the old word for look into OL; 'in' then sets it inside the French capital, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Pole Star, the bright star nearly above the north pole of the sky.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stop something is to check it

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect the cargo going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns STOP round since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots, as in 'pots of money', means loads or lots.

indicators.note: earliest in picks the first letter of the word the

parts.note: a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: An ancient relic dating from the earliest part of an event.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a surviving mark or remnant of something past, like a relic.

clue.text: Problem with joint? You'll need hour with it in warped stair

indicators.note: warped means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: hour gives HR

explanation.surface: A sufferer with a bad knee faces a crooked staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warped' is the anagram signal. In the answer the hour letter and the pronoun are not next to each other, so they cannot go in as one block: all three pieces are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the joints causing pain and stiffness is a disorder, a problem affecting joints.
